title: MCP server for camera tools + per-alert event.json artifact
context: Gate-alert split: the outer-loop agent (separate repo, MCP client) needs a stable API into the inner-loop pipeline (this repo). This PRD lands the inner side of that seam: an MCP server exposing read-only camera tools over stdio or HTTP, plus a per-alert event.json record so the outer agent can audit history without re-deriving it. Behavioral change to pipeline.run() = none. Tests = still all pass.
shipping_definition: infra/mcp_server.py registers a stdio MCP server with tools: camera_snapshot(camera_id) -> PNG bytes path, camera_last_events(camera_id, n=10) -> list[EventRecord], camera_health() -> dict, camera_list() -> list[{camera_id, display_name, model}]

pipeline.run() writes data/events/<alert_id>/event.json containing alert_id, camera_id, timestamps, gate verdict, vm1 result, vm2 result, match result, dropped reason (if any), and references to frame paths
event.json shape is the contract for the outer-loop agent; documented in docs/MCP-API.md
Existing 178 unit tests + 17 e2e tests still pass; no behavioral change to alerts reaching Telegram
MCP server is opt-in via env var FARMSURV_MCP_ENABLED=1 (1=ON, 0=OFF, default 0); launchd plist unchanged (operator rule: zero env vars in plist)
No new external dependency at runtime — stdlib `mcp` package only if already in pyproject.toml; otherwise a 100-line stdlib JSON-RPC shim over stdio
design_principles: Read-only tools first. camera_snapshot, camera_last_events, camera_health, camera_list. No write/mutation tools in this PRD — outer agent cannot mute cameras or enroll identities through MCP yet. That's a follow-up PRD (V2-069).

MCP server is a separate process from the listener. It reads data/events/ + ring buffers; it does not call pipeline.run() live. Stale-by-design (last 24h of events) so it can't accidentally re-trigger alerts.
event.json is the unit of truth for the outer agent. Frames + crops + diffs are referenced by path, not duplicated into the JSON.
stdio transport, not HTTP. Hermes and Pydantic AI both support stdio MCP cleanly. HTTP transport is a follow-up if a remote client ever needs it.
No Pydantic dependency added. Stdlib dataclasses for EventRecord; the shape is the contract; outer agent re-parses via JSON.

stories.title: Write per-alert event.json in pipeline.run()
scope: New module infra/event_record.py: EventRecord dataclass + write_event_record(alert_id, camera_id, stage_results) function

EventRecord fields: alert_id (str), camera_id (str), started_at (ISO8601), finished_at (ISO8601), gate (GateVerdict | None), vm1 (Vm1Result | None), vm2 (dict | None), match (MatchResult | None), dropped (str | None), frame_paths (list[Path]), artifact_dir (Path)
pipeline.run() calls write_event_record() once per alert, after the final stage (whether dropped or fully sent)
Atomic write: write to .tmp, fsync, rename — same pattern as existing JSONL audit
tests: Existing pipeline tests must continue to pass; event.json is a new side-effect, not a behavioral change

stories.title: Add infra/mcp_server.py with read-only camera tools over stdio
scope: infra/mcp_tools.py: pure functions — list_cameras(), get_health(), get_snapshot(camera_id), get_last_events(camera_id, n)
infra/mcp_server.py: stdio MCP server (mcp package or stdlib shim) exposing the four tools above
Tool input/output schemas documented as JSON Schema in tool descriptions
camera_snapshot reads the latest saved frame from data/frames/<camera>/ — does NOT pull live RTSP (that's the listener's job)
camera_last_events reads data/events/<camera>/*/event.json — last N, newest first
Gate behind FARMSURV_MCP_ENABLED=1; the module imports cleanly but registers no tools when 0
Standalone runnable: `python -m infra.mcp_server` starts the stdio server (for MCP client to spawn)

stories.title: Document MCP API contract for outer-loop consumers
scope: Document each tool: name, input schema, output schema, error cases, freshness guarantees
Reference the original design discussion: docs/original-design-discussion.md (in the gate-alert repo) is the design rationale; this file is the contract
Include a 'do not call from outer agent' section: list of things outer MUST NOT do (call live pipeline, mutate files, restart listener)
Cross-reference V2-069 (write tools) as a future extension

blocks: V2-069 (MCP write tools — outer-loop can mute/enroll)
estimated_complexity: small — three stories, additive changes, no pipeline behavior change
